ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: As shown in the figure <img="q_07905_001.png">, the three taxa M, N, and O share the characteristic of a white circle; this characteristic is not only present in their most recent common ancestor, but also present in an earlier ancestor ($*$). Therefore, the white circle is a shared ancestral character of these three taxa.

The tips of M, N, and O and their related branches/ancestral nodes are marked with white circle symbols; at a lower position in figure 3, beside an earlier ancestral node, a white circle can also be seen and is marked with *. At the continuing upward branch on the right side of figure 3, a black circle appears, and the tips of P, Q, and R are also marked as black circles. In phylogenetic terminology, a shared character present in an earlier ancestor corresponds to an "ancestral character." Therefore the white circle should be determined as Ancestor.
